Elaborate this line a bit. In addition, let's point to the PLDM commit and add testing details.

Updated the commit message.
IT is dependent on PLDM changes, will add the test results once it's done.
Acknowledged
Should we error out if subtree's size is > 1?
Ack, that looks to be the correct behavior. Updated the same in the commit message as well.
Do we need this check?

The empty check is necessary due to the introduction of std::optional for the target field.
We need this check to distinguish between empty targets (pass nullopt) and one target.
Can we even have targets size > 1 here havong done the other checks that occur before?

No, it's not possible because we already validated it.
The current design passes a vector of targets to processUpdateRequest but converts it to a single target for getSwInfo.
But this code can be extended in future when multiple targets are supported
Why is this change needed?

multipart->targets is now a std::optional<std::vector<std::string>> to represent that the "Targets" field in the Multipart update request is optional.

When the "Targets" field is not provided, multipart->targets is nullopt, but processUpdateRequest still expects a valid vector.
CI failure is unrelated to this patch.
nit: Update the commit message to be readable.
Acknowledged
With this patch MultiPart API would accept single target or No Targets?
It would support both single target and no target.
Can this be mapped to a standard RF error code other than InternalError?

When there's no software object creating Update interface, it should be a server-side fault, not a bad request therefore used internalError for this case.

If there was a target specified, we could have used `resourceNotFound`

How about `serviceTemporarilyUnavailable`? But it expects a retry time.

Let me know if you have any other suggestions
I am fine with either `internalError` or `resourceNotFound`. `resourceNotFound` may be better option here as the resource to facilitate Update is not found.
Is there any impact on this with the existing flow?

The code has always assumed that any software object implementing the Version interface would also implement the Update interface, since it calls StartUpdate on that same object.
I don’t see any impact from this change.
nit: DBus -> D-Bus
Acknowledged
Changing the namespace to "/xyz/openbmc_project" from "/xyz/openbmc_project/software" to accomodate StartUpdate at service level?
Yes.

How would this co-exist with the existing software update design? In that case, there are going to be multiple StartUpdate interfaces, how do you know you are choosing the right one? There was a version of your design where an explicit Multi-partManager interface was proposed. Please follow up on that.

The original bmcweb implementation does not support multi-target updates, and this patch does not introduce that capability either.

* Single target specified: The behavior remains unchanged; updates proceed as before.

* No targets specified: The update is triggered on the entity implementing StartUpdate. However, this only works if there is exactly one such entity. If multiple entities implement StartUpdate, bmcweb will raise an error.

In short, multi-target updates are still not supported under the current software update design. 

On top of that, PLDM updates have been broken for the past six months since the switch to StartUpdate in bmcweb.

> The original bmcweb implementation does not support multi-target updates, and this patch does not introduce that capability either.
> 
> * Single target specified: The behavior remains unchanged; updates proceed as before.
> 
> * No targets specified: The update is triggered on the entity implementing StartUpdate. However, this only works if there is exactly one such entity. If multiple entities implement StartUpdate, bmcweb will raise an error.
> 

I am not referring to multi targets in the Redfish URI list. I am referring to different updaters exposing the StartUpdate interface which is the current design. You are picking the very first StartUpdate interface how would that co-exist with the current design. Please work on your interfaces in the design and get consensus on that.

> In short, multi-target updates are still not supported under the current software update design. 
> 
> On top of that, PLDM updates have been broken for the past six months since the switch to StartUpdate in bmcweb.

PLDM updates never worked properly. That was some hacked up code copied to PLDMd from phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt which used to look for the images from the same place as BMC updater as BMCWeb used to put it in /tmp/images dir. One of the two daemons used to win race for image, delete it from /tmp/images directory and then drop the image if it was not intended for it. So, that was never the solution which should have been put up upstream in the first go. FYI: This was the patch which added that change to PLDMd https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/pldm/+/45952. Lets not do similar sort of hack solution again.

(CC @patrick@stwcx.xyz).

@paligill@gmail.com with the current design the Redfish user must specify a Target, and Rajeev's patch here doesn't impact that flow. I'm not sure I understand your concern. The code doesn't pick the first StartUpdate interface - it picks the only StartUpdate interface (when there is just one - the pldmd app level update) and no Targets are specified.

> @paligill@gmail.com with the current design the Redfish user must specify a Target, and Rajeev's patch here doesn't impact that flow. I'm not sure I understand your concern. The code doesn't pick the first StartUpdate interface - it picks the only StartUpdate interface (when there is just one - the pldmd app level update) and no Targets are specified.

My concern is arising from the fact that you are defaulting the behavior to a Multipart image parser by using the same Update interface as a device level updater. What would be the interface if multiple targets are supplied. There is no consensus on the interface for Multipart image parser yet. I see the design from Tom (where he was proposing a Multipart Manager interface) totally changed from what i reviewed last time. I have provided comments on that.

Also, i see this patch from Rajeev 
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/82235. Looks like design changes are being put up in bits and pieces.

First there needs to be a consensus on what would be the Dbus interface for Multipart updater. So, first lets get that.

The design changed (Tom will respond) because you were pushing back on multipart manager. Tom had also pushed a PDI that you pushed back on and then stopped giving feedback on (https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/78905). You were fine with the current design that solves only part of PLDM update (single component update), and doesn't address component ordering, but are agaist incremental updates to the design that attempts to solve component ordering?

Would appreciate timely/actionable feedback (on the design doc) so that we can avoid going in circles for months.

This patch and Tom's design doc is incrementally adding to the current design pldmd multipart support with component ordering where a user doesn't need to specify targets. I don't think that needs a new PDI. StartUpdate can be implemented at app/top-level.

Multiple Targets is not solved yet but neither does the current design/code/patches on Gerrit solve it (keeping conponent ordering intact).
As mentioned here and elsewhere, patch addresses bundle updates with no Targets, via a new PDI to identify MultipartUpdate.
Please add reference to the design which is under discussion.
